name: ducati_desmosedici_stradale
label: Ducati Desmosedici Stradale 1103 cc 90° V4 (Panigale V4)
based_on: Ducati Desmosedici Stradale 1103 cc V4, Panigale V4 / V4 S, 2018

sources.what: MCNews.com.au reproduction of Ducati's long Desmosedici Stradale technical press release (September 2017). Manufacturer text reproduced by a motorcycle news site: rod length, crank pin offset, firing points, valve sizes, intake system.

Total Motorcycle reproduction of the same Ducati press release including the 'Main technical data' list (bore, stroke, compression, power, torque, 14,000 rpm). Used to cross-check MCNews; the firing-order and 101.8 mm passages appear identically.
Motorcycle.com news report on the engine unveiling; independently restates 70 deg offset, firing points 0/90/290/380 and which cylinders fire when.
CycleOnline reproduction of the short version of the Ducati release; cross-check of power, torque, counter-rotating crank and 70 deg offset.
Ducati Panigale V4 / V4 S / Speciale specification sheet (PDF), hosted by a US parts retailer. Manufacturer data for the production bike: 157.5 kW, 124 Nm, 4-2-1-2 exhaust.
Bennetts BikeSocial interview with Ducati's engine development staff; gives the firing points against cylinder numbers 1-4 and the torque plateau.

notes: Sourced (Ducati press material): bore, stroke, compression ratio 14, 90-degree V4, two crank pins offset 70 degrees, ignition at 0, 90, 290 and 380 degrees (intervals 90-200-90-340) in the order front then rear on the alternator side, then front then rear on the clutch side, rod length 101.8 mm, four valves per cylinder, valve diameters 34/27.5 mm, 52 mm equivalent throttle bodies, 4-2-1-2 exhaust, 14,000 rpm maximum speed, published power and torque. Cylinder order in this file: 1 front alternator side, 2 rear alternator side, 3 front clutch side, 4 rear clutch side (Ducati's own numbering was not found). That each crank pin carries the front and rear cylinder of one side is implied by the release, not stated; with it the pins come out shared and 70 degrees apart. Estimated, not sourced: all cam timing and lift (nothing is published; 242 degrees intake and 252 exhaust at 1 mm lift on 106-degree centres, 12.0 and 10.25 mm lift, tuned to the published figures); intake length (0.26 m; the real engine has two-stage variable-height horns and the format has one fixed length) and diameter; exhaust primary lengths (0.30 m) and diameters, which cylinders pair at the 4-2 junction (the two front and the two rear assumed), secondary, silencer and tailpipe dimensions; idle speed (1400 rpm); flywheel inertia; friction_scale 0.6, heat_q 2.7e6 and burn_scale 0.7, the first two at the end of their allowed range. Known gap: about 16% low on power at 13,000 rpm. The model's friction rises with the square of engine speed regardless of stroke, which costs a short-stroke engine over 4 bar at that speed even at the lowest allowed friction_scale. The counter-rotating crankshaft has no effect in this model.

vehicle.name: Ducati Panigale V4 (2018)
vehicle.notes: Base Panigale V4; Ducati's kerb weight (the V4 S is 195 kg). Ducati gives the primary only as 1.80:1, so final_drive is 1.80 x chain 41:16. top_speed_kmh is Young Machine's GPS-measured 306 km/h for the V4 S, which has the same engine and gearing and was on the 14,500 rpm limiter; no figure was found for the base bike. wheel_radius_m is calculated from the tyre size.
